slots.caption: Figure 1.1 — Searching a floor properly, in squares, left to right.
slots.alt: A man kneels in debris patting the floor in neat squares while catastrophe unfolds unnoticed in the window behind him.
slots.prompt: A cartoonish bean-bodied older man in a flat cap and long tarp coat, on his hands and knees on a debris-strewn floor, patting the boards with both oversized hands, head down, cheerful and entirely absorbed. Faint flat orange grid squares are chalked on the floorboards and one square is ticked off. Behind him a simple rectangular window frame shows a flat skyline of tilted buildings and smoke columns, drawn small. He is turned away from it. Minimal props: an overturned chair, scattered angular glass shards, a dropped cup. Orange used only for the floor grid and the ticks.

slots.caption: Figure 1.3 — The whole method, as first written down.
slots.alt: A tiny three-box flowchart of the three questions, drawn in pen on the back of a creased envelope.
slots.prompt: A creased, slightly torn paper envelope lying flat, drawn in flat black line art, with a hand-drawn three-box flowchart scrawled on its back in the same ink. Three plain rectangles connected by downward arrows, each containing a simple glyph instead of words — a drop for bleeding, a pair of lungs for air, a small stick figure with a question mark over it. One orange thumbprint smudge at the envelope's corner. Loose, hasty, marginal. No background scenery.

slots.caption: Figure 1.2 — The order to think in: three minutes of air, three hours of shelter, three days of water, three weeks of food. The numbers are a mnemonic, not a timetable.
slots.alt: A four-tread staircase diagram, the treads numbered one to four for air, shelter, water and food.
slots.prompt: A clean four-tread staircase diagram seen in flat side profile, drawn as a civil-defence pamphlet figure. The treads descend left to right and are labelled in order with orange callout numerals 1 to 4 in orange circles: tread 1 air, tread 2 shelter, tread 3 water, tread 4 food. Each tread carries a tiny flat glyph above it — a pair of lungs, a simple lean-to roof, a water drop, a tin can. Generous empty cream space around the staircase, single subject, no background scenery, no text beyond the callout numerals.

slots.caption: Figure 2.1 — The two errors, drawn to scale. 1 too early. 2 too late.
slots.alt: Two panels side by side; in one a cheerfully bored man sits on a hill with a packed bag, in the other only a pair of empty boots stands in a doorway.
slots.prompt: A two-panel comparison drawn as a flat civil-defence pamphlet figure, divided by a single vertical black rule. Left panel: a cartoonish bean-bodied man in a flat cap and long tarp coat sitting on a small bare hummock beside a canvas two-buckled bag, chin on fist, cheerfully bored, swinging one boot, one orange callout numeral 1 in an orange circle beside him. Right panel: an empty plain door frame with a single pair of worn boots standing neatly in the opening and nobody in them, one orange callout numeral 2 in an orange circle beside the frame. Both panels otherwise empty cream ground, no background scenery, no text beyond the two callout numerals.

slots.caption: Figure 2.3 — The author's first bag, on its only journey.
slots.alt: A man crouched under an absurdly overpacked bag with a cast-iron pan lashed to it, halfway up a staircase, cheerful.
slots.prompt: A cartoonish bean-bodied older man in a flat cap and long tarp coat, seen from behind and three-quarter, bent far forward halfway up a plain flight of stairs under a canvas two-buckled bag with a patch on its lower left corner, grotesquely overstuffed so the fabric bulges and the buckles strain. Far too many objects are lashed to the outside with cord — a large cast-iron frying pan, a kettle, a folding stool, a stack of books, a mantel clock, a single boot with no pair. His posture is cheerful and unbothered, one hand giving a small wave. One orange cord binding is the only orange in the figure. Empty cream ground, no background scenery beyond the stairs, no text.

slots.caption: Figure 2.2 — The bag, cut away. 1 water, in more than one container, low and against the back panel. 2 light, plus a spare on different batteries. 3 dry warm layer, bagged dry. 4 documents, copied. 5 medication, with the written names. 6 one good knife.
slots.alt: Cutaway diagram of a packed canvas shoulder bag with six numbered contents.
slots.prompt: Cutaway diagram of a single canvas bag with two buckles and a patch on its lower left corner, shown in flat side profile with the near wall of the bag removed so the contents are visible, stacked in clear separated compartments. Six contents, each marked with an orange callout numeral in an orange circle: 1 two water bottles of different shapes at the bottom, 2 a head-strap lamp and a small second torch, 3 a folded layer of clothing inside a sealed pouch, 4 a flat folded document wallet, 5 a small tin of pills with a folded paper list beside it, 6 a single sheathed knife along the spine of the bag. Heavy water low and close to the back panel. Single subject, generous empty cream space around the bag, no background scenery, no text beyond the six callout numerals.

slots.caption: Figure 3.3 — Things the author has splinted with. 1 fence pale. 2 road sign. 3 flatbread, twice. 4 oar. 5 regrettable.
slots.alt: A cheerful man standing with an absurd assortment of objects strapped to all four limbs as splints, including a road sign and a guitar neck.
slots.prompt: A cartoonish bean-bodied older man in a flat cap and long tarp coat, standing facing forward with arms held out from his sides, grinning, entirely pleased with himself. Strapped to his limbs with cord and torn cloth are absurdly mismatched splints, each tagged with an orange callout numeral in an orange circle: 1 a wooden fence pale on his left forearm, 2 a large flat diamond road sign bound to his right thigh, 3 a thick rolled flatbread lashed to his left shin, 4 a long boat oar running the length of his right arm and far past his hand, 5 the neck of a guitar strapped to his left thigh. The splints are oversized and poorly matched and he stands stiffly because of it. Orange used only for the five callout numerals and one cord binding. Empty cream ground, single subject, no background scenery, no text beyond the numerals.

slots.caption: Figure 3.1 — Direct pressure and packing. 1 heel of the hand, one spot. 2 second hand stacked. 3 material fed fully in. 4 both hands on top, held still.
slots.alt: Two-panel diagram of hands demonstrating stacked direct pressure and wound packing on a plain limb outline, no wound or blood depicted.
slots.prompt: A two-panel instructional diagram in flat black line art on cream, divided by a single vertical rule, drawn as a civil-defence pamphlet figure. Left panel: a plain featureless limb outline lying horizontally, with one hand placed heel-down on a small folded square of cloth and the second hand stacked flat on top of it, forearms shown vertical and locked; orange callout numeral 1 in an orange circle at the lower hand, numeral 2 at the upper hand. Right panel: the same plain limb outline with a small plain oval marked on it and a single index finger shown feeding a folded strip of dressing material into the oval, a coil of further dressing waiting beside it; orange callout numeral 3 at the finger, numeral 4 at a pair of stacked hands drawn pressing above. Hands and plain limb outlines only, no faces, no figures, no wound detail, no red, no depiction of blood of any kind. Orange used only for the four callout numerals. Generous empty cream space, no background scenery, no text beyond the numerals.

slots.caption: Figure 3.2 — Tourniquet placement. 1 the wound. 2 the strap, high and above the joint. 3 the windlass, turned until bleeding stops. 4 the time it went on.
slots.alt: Diagram of a plain limb outline with a wide strap and windlass placed high above a marked wound, with a blank time label tied to the strap.
slots.prompt: An instructional diagram in flat black line art on cream, drawn as a civil-defence pamphlet figure. A single plain featureless leg outline shown in flat profile from hip to foot, with the knee joint indicated by a thin dashed line only. A small plain oval low on the shin carries orange callout numeral 1. A wide flat strap is drawn encircling the thigh well above the dashed knee line, carrying orange callout numeral 2. A short rod threaded through the strap and shown mid-turn carries orange callout numeral 3, with a small curved arrow indicating the turn. A small rectangular label tied to the strap carries orange callout numeral 4 and is blank. Plain limb outline only, no wound detail, no red, no depiction of blood of any kind. Orange used only for the four callout numerals and the one arrow. Generous empty cream space, single subject, no background scenery, no text beyond the numerals.

slots.caption: Figure 4.1 — The Ninth Hand's water ceremony. 1 the oration. 2 the crack.
slots.alt: A solemn crowd of robed figures presses handprints onto a cistern wall while a man orates from its lid; at the frame's edge a man with a bucket stares at the lid's crack.
slots.prompt: A cartoonish flat black line drawing on cream. Centre: a low round stone cistern with a flat lid, its wall covered in overlapping pressed handprints, a tall thin robed man standing on the lid with both arms raised mid-oration, carrying orange callout numeral 1 in an orange circle beside him. A jagged crack runs across the lid under his feet, carrying orange callout numeral 2 in an orange circle. Around the cistern a dozen robed figures stand extremely solemn with heads bowed and one hand each raised. At the far right edge of the frame, turned fully away from the crowd and facing the cistern, a cartoonish bean-bodied older man in a flat cap and long tarp coat holds a full bucket in both hands and peers down at the crack with an expression of mild professional annoyance. Orange used only for the two callout numerals. Empty cream ground, no background scenery, no text beyond the numerals.

slots.caption: Figure 4.2 — The barrel filter, cut away. 1 cloth. 2 charcoal. 3 fine sand. 4 gravel over the outlet. 5 the stage everyone skips.
slots.alt: Cutaway diagram of a cut barrel packed in three layers with a cloth over the top and a spout feeding a lidded pot on a fire below.
slots.prompt: Cutaway diagram in flat black line art on cream, drawn as a civil-defence pamphlet figure. A cut barrel standing upright with its near wall removed to show three distinct packed layers, each hatched differently and separated by a horizontal line. A square of doubled cloth is stretched over the barrel's open mouth with water being poured onto it, carrying orange callout numeral 1 in an orange circle. The top layer inside is coarse granular charcoal, numeral 2. The middle layer is fine stippled sand, drawn thickest of the three, numeral 3. The bottom layer is large rounded gravel, numeral 4, sitting over a short spout in the barrel's lower wall. Below the spout a drip falls into a plain lidded pot on a small flat fire, carrying orange callout numeral 5. Single subject, generous empty cream space, no background scenery, no text beyond the five numerals.

slots.caption: Figure 4.3 — Treating it. 1 clear. 2 cloudy. 3 strain and settle. 4 boil one minute, three up high. 5 or treat, stood thirty minutes.
slots.alt: A flowchart branching from a clear jar and a cloudy jar into a straining and settling step and then into a boiling pot or a dosed and covered jar.
slots.prompt: A decision flowchart in flat black line art on cream, drawn as a civil-defence pamphlet figure, using glyphs only and no words. Two plain rectangular boxes at the top: the left box holds a jar with a clean empty interior and two straight ripple lines, carrying orange callout numeral 1 in an orange circle; the right box holds an identical jar drawn with dense stipple throughout, carrying orange callout numeral 2. A downward arrow from the right box leads to a middle box showing a square of cloth over a funnel above a tall jar with a thick settled band of stipple at its bottom, carrying orange callout numeral 3. Arrows from the left box and from the middle box converge and then split into two boxes at the bottom: the left-hand one shows a lidded pot with vigorous bubbles over a small flat fire, numeral 4; the right-hand one shows a covered jar with a single drop poised above it and a plain circular clock face alongside, numeral 5. Clean orthogonal connecting arrows. Orange used only for the five callout numerals. Generous empty cream space, no background scenery, no text beyond the numerals.

slots.caption: Figure 5.3 — My first shelter. Eleven days, slept nine, never once got warm.
slots.alt: An enormous, beautifully built shelter with its builder asleep on the ground outside the door.
slots.prompt: A cartoonish flat black line drawing on cream. Centre and filling most of the frame, an enormous, elaborate, beautifully constructed lean-to shelter of lashed poles and neatly layered thatch, drawn with obvious craftsmanship, far too large, with a wide gaping doorway through which a few small flat snowflakes are drifting and settling on the floor inside. In the bottom left corner, outside and beside the doorway, a cartoonish bean-bodied older man in a flat cap, cracked spectacles and a long tarp coat lies curled on the bare ground, fast asleep, with a small contented smile and an expression of mild cheerful regret. Two or three small orange breath-puffs rise from him. Orange used only for the breath-puffs. Empty cream ground, no background scenery, no text.

slots.caption: Figure 5.1 — Insulation, in order. 1 the thin layer against the skin. 2 the loft, which is only trapped air. 3 the shell that keeps wind and rain out of 2. 4 what goes under you, which outranks all three.
slots.alt: Cross-section diagram of three clothing layers over a torso, with a thick emphasised band of ground insulation beneath.
slots.prompt: A cross-section diagram in flat black line art on cream, drawn as a civil-defence pamphlet figure. A simplified torso seen in section at the top, wrapped in three concentric bands drawn at clearly different thicknesses and hatched differently: a thin innermost band carrying orange callout numeral 1 in an orange circle, a thick fluffy middle band of loose stipple carrying orange callout numeral 2, and a smooth outermost band carrying orange callout numeral 3, with small arrows of wind and rain glancing off it. Beneath the torso, a deep horizontal band of loose compressed vegetation drawn thicker than any clothing layer and outlined entirely in orange, carrying orange callout numeral 4 in an orange circle, separating the figure from a flat hatched ground line below. Small downward arrows run from the figure into the ground line to show heat leaving. Single subject, generous empty cream space, no background scenery, no text beyond the four numerals.

slots.caption: Figure 5.2 — Heat exhaustion against heat stroke. 1 the skin. 2 pulse and breathing. 3 the mind, which is the row that decides. 4 what you do about it.
slots.alt: A two-column comparison chart of heat exhaustion and heat stroke, the mental-state row boxed and emphasised.
slots.prompt: A two-column comparison chart in flat black line art on cream, drawn as a civil-defence pamphlet figure, using glyphs only and no words. Two equal columns divided by a single vertical rule, crossed by four horizontal rows. Row 1 carries orange callout numeral 1 in an orange circle and shows, left, a face with heavy sweat droplets and flat shading for pallor, and right, a face with radiating heat lines and no droplets. Row 2 carries numeral 2 and shows, left, a shallow fluttering waveform, and right, a tall spiking waveform. Row 3 carries numeral 3, is enclosed in a heavy orange box drawn around the whole row, and shows, left, a head in profile with a clear steady spiral inside it, and right, a head in profile with a broken scribbled tangle inside it. Row 4 carries numeral 4 and shows, left, a reclining figure under a simple shade canopy beside a cup, and right, a figure immersed to the neck in a tub of water with wavy-line fanning arrows. Generous empty cream space, no background scenery, no text beyond the four numerals.

slots.caption: Figure 6.1 — Arno Bligh's pantry. Four hundred pounds of beans and one pot.
slots.alt: A huge, immaculately stacked pantry of bean sacks with a single pot on the floor, as a man arrives in the doorway with another sack.
slots.prompt: A cartoonish flat black line drawing on cream. Filling most of the frame, an enormous pantry wall of neatly stacked bulging sacks, piled shoulder-high in tidy rows receding to the back of a long narrow room, drawn with obvious pride of stacking, every sack identical and untouched. On the bare floorboards in the centre foreground, one small dented cooking pot, alone, drawn in orange. Orange used only for the pot. In the right-hand doorway, seen from behind and in three-quarter profile, a cartoonish bean-bodied older man in a flat cap and long tarp coat arriving with another full sack on one shoulder, head turned down and away toward his own feet, not looking at the stacks or the pot. Generous empty cream space above the stacks, no background scenery, no text.

slots.caption: Figure 6.3 — Fuel into time. 1 the soak, water thrown away. 2 lid on, ten minutes at a hard boil. 3 packed in dry hay, under as well as over. 4 unopened.
slots.alt: Four numbered panels showing soaking beans, a lidded pot at a hard boil, the pot packed in straw inside a crate, and the closed crate standing untouched.
slots.prompt: Four equal square panels in a single row, divided by thin vertical rules, in flat black line art on cream, drawn as a civil-defence pamphlet figure, glyphs only and no words. Panel 1 carries orange callout numeral 1 in an orange circle and shows a wide bowl of beans covered by water to well above them, with a small orange curved arrow tipping a second bowl of cloudy water away to one side. Panel 2 carries numeral 2 and shows a pot with a weighted lid clamped down over a simple fire of three logs, vigorous large bubbles drawn inside the pot and short steam wisps escaping at the lid rim. Panel 3 carries numeral 3 and shows a cutaway of a square crate with the same lidded pot nested inside it, surrounded on all sides by dense loose straw stippling drawn at equal and clearly generous thickness beneath the pot as above and beside it, with a folded blanket laid over the top. Panel 4 carries numeral 4 and shows the same crate closed, standing alone with no fire anywhere near it, a small orange crescent moon and sun pair above it to indicate long elapsed time, and a flat orange bar across the lid to indicate it is not to be opened. Orange used only for the four numerals, the tipping arrow, the time glyphs and the bar. Generous empty cream space, no background scenery, no text beyond the four numerals.

slots.caption: Figure 6.2 — Three tins not to open. 1 the domed end. 2 the leak and rust. 3 the damaged seam. A tin with none of them proves nothing.
slots.alt: Three cans in a row, each with one defect circled in orange — a bulging lid, a leaking rusted side, and a dented seam.
slots.prompt: Three identical plain cylindrical food tins in a row on a flat baseline, drawn in flat black line art on cream as a civil-defence pamphlet figure, each tin unlabelled and smooth-sided. The left tin has its top end clearly domed and swollen upward, ringed in orange and carrying orange callout numeral 1 in an orange circle. The middle tin has a patch of rough stippled rust low on its side with two small drips running from it down to a small pool on the baseline, ringed in orange and carrying orange callout numeral 2. The right tin has a deep crease and dent running across the rolled seam where the lid meets the body, with short radiating stress lines, ringed in orange and carrying orange callout numeral 3. Orange used only for the three rings, the three numerals and the drips. Generous empty cream space between and above the tins, no background scenery, no text beyond the three numerals.
